design_gotchas.title: CRITICAL Mixed Legacy (CSO:DLN) vs New Chip (CSO:RFB) Silicon Lottery on Non-M3 OPN
design_gotchas.detail: Table 8-1 (p.28) reveals non-M3 TPS79333DBVR reels can ship EITHER Legacy Chip (CSO:DLN) or New Chip (CSO:RFB) with major electrical divergence: Pin 4 changes from NR to NC, noise doubles (33 -> 69 uVRMS), 10 kHz PSRR plunges 21 dB (70 -> 49 dB), startup slows 10x (50 -> 500 us), max IQ jumps 4.5x (220 -> 1000 uA), VEN(HI) shifts (1.7 -> 0.85 V), UVLO shifts (2.25 -> 1.32 V), and only New Chip adds 120 Ohm active discharge. Use TPS79333DBVRM3 to lock New Chip or migrate to TPS7A20 for low noise.

design_gotchas.title: Never Ground Pin 4 (NC/NR) Unless Locked to M3 New-Chip Silicon
design_gotchas.detail: Although Pin 4 is NC on New Chip silicon, Legacy Chip units connect Pin 4 to the internal 1.22 V bandgap reference via a 250 kOhm resistor (p.14, p.24). Grounding Pin 4 (as permitted on NC-pin LDOs like TLV702/AP2204) collapses VOUT on Legacy Chip reels! Keep a 0.01 uF low-leakage CNR cap to GND or leave Pin 4 floating if mixed reels are possible; never load Pin 4 resistively or inductively (p.25).

design_gotchas.title: New Chip Requires 1 uF CIN (Up From 0.1 uF Legacy) & 2.2 uF COUT for > 100 mA Load
design_gotchas.detail: Table 5.3 (p.4) and Section 7.2.2.2 (p.23–24) require >= 1 uF ceramic CIN for New Chip stability (vs 0.1 uF on Legacy Chip) and >= 2.2 uF low-ESR ceramic COUT for 200 mA operation (1 uF only permitted below 100 mA). Do not copy legacy 0.1 uF CIN designs onto New Chip reels without upgrading CIN to 1 uF.

design_gotchas.title: No Reverse-Current Protection & Datasheet Table 4-1 Pin Numbering Trap (OUT=5 vs 6)
design_gotchas.detail: Section 6.3.6 (p.17–18) warns that VOUT > VIN + 0.3 V forces damaging reverse body-diode current (limit <= 5% of rated IOUT = 10 mA or add an external Schottky). Also note Table 4-1 (p.3) prints DBV pin 6 for OUT (6-pin adjustable TPS79301) whereas Figure 4-1 confirms 5-pin fixed TPS79333DBVR has OUT on Pin 5.

typical_use_cases: Low-dropout (112 mV typ at 200 mA) 3.6–5.5 V to 3.3 V analog and peripheral rails in SOT-23-5
Drop-in maintenance and second-source support for legacy RF/audio boards populated with a 10 nF Pin-4 NR bypass cap
Compact 200 mA 3.3 V rails in TVs, printers, and building automation (upgrade to TPS7A20 for new ultra-low-noise designs)
Candidate drop-in comparison against SOT-23-5 BYPASS-pin LDOs (LP2985, TPS736, CAT6219) after verifying Legacy vs New die
engineering_summary: The Texas Instruments TPS79333DBVR is a 200 mA fixed 3.3 V (±2% over -40°C to +125°C) low-dropout (112 mV typ / 180 mV max at 200 mA) PMOS LDO in a 5-pin DBV SOT-23-5 package (1=IN, 2=GND, 3=EN active high, 4=NC/NR, 5=OUT, RθJA = 182.3 °C/W). Operating from 2.7 V to 5.5 V, non-M3 TPS79333DBVR reels may ship either Legacy Chip (CSO:DLN: Pin 4 NR bypass, 33 uVRMS noise, 70 dB 10 kHz PSRR, 50 us startup, 170 uA IQ, 6 V abs max) or New Chip (CSO:RFB: Pin 4 NC, 69 uVRMS noise, 49 dB 10 kHz PSRR, 500 us startup, 250 uA typ / 1000 uA max IQ, 6.5 V abs max, active discharge). Never ground Pin 4 on non-M3 boards and use >= 1 uF CIN and >= 2.2 uF COUT.
